papers.title: The Monitoring Paradox: Frontal Electroencephalography Reveals Profound Cortical Depression Despite Cardiovascular Stability in Dogs Undergoing Tibial Plateau Leveling Osteotomy with Isoflurane Anesthesia and Multimodal Analgesic Protocols.
papers.summary: In 21 dogs undergoing tibial plateau leveling osteotomy under isoflurane anesthesia, frontal EEG and parasympathetic tone activity revealed profound cortical depression despite stable cardiorespiratory indices; fentanyl produced deeper suppression and more Double-Low states than epidural morphine, with dysphoric recovery in 9 of 21 dogs.

papers.title: Impact of Recording Conditions and Feature Fusion on Dementia Classification Using Spectral, Entropy, and Complexity EEG Features.
papers.summary: This study compared spectral, entropy, and complexity EEG features for classifying Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment, and healthy controls under eyes-closed and eyes-open conditions, finding that feature fusion benefits were task-dependent; spectral features were best for AD-HC and AD-MCI, while entropy or combined features were best for MCI-HC depending on condition.

papers.title: Multidomain Electroencephalography Biomarker Fusion for Machine Learning-Based Dementia Classification.
papers.summary: Evaluated multidomain resting-state EEG biomarkers (RMS, power spectral density, entropy) plus demographic features for machine learning classification of Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and healthy controls in 88 participants using a Random Forest classifier with explainable AI. The full model achieved 96% training and 92% test accuracy, and removing entropy features increased test accuracy to 94%.

papers.title: FRFNet: a fatigue-robust EEG-EMG fusion network for hand movement intention recognition.
papers.summary: Proposes FRFNet, a fatigue-robust EEG-EMG fusion network with multiscale temporal convolution, dual-path fatigue disentanglement, and fatigue-aware adaptive gating for hand movement intention recognition. Under synthetic EMG degradation up to 90%, FRFNet achieved 60.0% within-subject accuracy and 57.0% leave-one-subject-out accuracy, outperforming comparison methods, with 1.166 million parameters and 5.321 ms mean inference latency.

papers.title: Study on VDT fatigue detection for complex industrial control room operators based on multi-modal fusion.
papers.summary: Analyzed subjective and objective physiological data, including EEG and eye-tracking, from 16 operators before and after shifts to detect visual display terminal fatigue in complex industrial control rooms. A TabNet-based multimodal fusion model achieved an accuracy of 0.881 and F1-score of 0.919 on a small-sample field dataset, showing favorable classification performance relative to traditional comparison models.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in epilepsy diagnosis: Clinical readiness, failure modes, and standards for Implementation.
papers.summary: Reviews the clinical readiness, failure modes, and implementation standards of artificial intelligence for epilepsy diagnosis across modalities such as EEG, MRI, wearables, natural language processing, and multimodal models, organized around four diagnostic questions. It reports that automated EEG interpretation is the most mature domain but false-positive epileptiform activity and automation bias remain safety concerns, and argues the decisive transition is from algorithmic performance to external validation, calibration, and clinical utility.

papers.title: Groove strength is associated with cortical β suppression and tapping stability.
papers.summary: Tested whether groove ratings during rhythmic music are linked to motor cortical beta suppression and tapping stability in 28 healthy adults tapping to drum patterns of varying syncopation while EEG was recorded. Groove ratings showed an inverted U-shape peaking at intermediate syncopation, and higher-groove patterns were associated with lower beta power during both synchronization and continuation phases and with minimum tapping variability at the same syncopation level.

papers.title: From Signal Stacking to Dynamic Coupling: A Critical Review of Wearable EEG-EMG Fusion Brain-Computer Interfaces for Stroke Rehabilitation.
papers.summary: This critical review examines wearable EEG-EMG fusion brain-computer interfaces for stroke rehabilitation, arguing that conventional fusion treats cross-modal relationships as fixed and proposing a shift toward dynamic brain-muscle coupling methods such as time-resolved corticomuscular coherence, phase locking, and dynamic graph connectivity, while identifying barriers to clinical translation.

papers.title: Low-frequency oscillations in frontocentral EEG responses associated with auditory motion processing.
papers.summary: This study investigated oscillatory dynamics underlying auditory motion processing in a delayed motion paradigm with EEG. It found that inter-trial phase coherence (ITC) is highly sensitive to velocity, with response magnitudes following a hyperbolic decline as a function of the 1-degree shift time, and latency increasing linearly with 1-degree shift time, indicating common temporal integration mechanisms across evoked and oscillatory responses.

papers.title: A novel multi-modal fusion framework based on simultaneous EEG-fNIRS for the classification of working memory loads.
papers.summary: The study proposed a novel multi-modal fusion framework based on simultaneous EEG-fNIRS for classifying working memory loads. Experimental results showed that bilinear common spatial pattern (BCSP) and envelope extraction significantly impacted classification accuracy, and feature-level fusion via element-wise addition and decision-level fusion via majority voting were superior to other methods.

papers.title: Comparison of amyloid-β, total tau and phospho-tau in clinical AD patients with and without epileptiform EEG patterns.
papers.summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed associations between interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) and CSF AD markers in 26 clinical AD patients. It observed that patients with IEDs or EEG background slowing had significantly lower phospho-tau levels than those without, and phospho-tau levels correlated with dominant posterior EEG frequencies, suggesting an unexpected inverse relationship.

papers.title: PDC-Net: A Prefrontal Dual-Channel Network with Gated Mamba Interaction for Cross-Subject Visual Attentional State Decoding.
papers.summary: PDC-Net, a prefrontal dual-channel EEG network with gated Mamba interaction, was developed for cross-subject decoding of visual sustained attention (VSA) and visual internally directed cognition (VIDC). Under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation with dual-channel Fp1/Fp2 EEG, PDC-Net achieved 76.76% average accuracy, the highest among 11 compared models, while balancing performance and computational cost.

papers.title: FSC-BiMamba: A Dual-Branch Bidirectional Mamba Network for Frontal Sparse-Channel EEG Depression Detection.
papers.summary: The paper proposes FSC-BiMamba, a dual-branch bidirectional Mamba network for subject-independent window-level depression detection from frontal sparse-channel EEG, integrating time-frequency maps and frequency-domain statistical descriptors via adaptive token fusion and cross-window context, achieving accuracies of 82.70% on MODMA and 84.55% on Mumtaz2016.

papers.title: Chronic pain and oscillatory neuroplasticity: Review on impaired compensatory network responses in resting-state electroencephalography.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized resting-state EEG functional connectivity studies in chronic pain, identifying consistent frequency-specific abnormalities in theta, alpha, beta, and gamma bands. It proposed a theoretical oscillatory neuroplasticity framework that organizes these alterations as an imbalance across learning, maintenance, stabilization, and fast plasticity systems.

papers.title: Resting-State 40 Hz EEG Activity Before and After Single-Session Non-Flickering 40 Hz Light Stimulation in Cognitively Normal Older Adults: An Uncontrolled Pilot Study.
papers.summary: This uncontrolled pilot study examined resting-state 40 Hz EEG activity before and after a single 60-minute session of non-flickering 40 Hz light stimulation in 16 cognitively normal older adults. After FDR correction, 38–42 Hz relative power increased in central and right temporal regions post-stimulation, with the right temporal increase also significant in absolute-power sensitivity analysis, though findings remain preliminary due to the small uncontrolled design.

papers.title: Knowledge-Guided Deep Learning with Clinical EEG Biomarkers for Automated Dementia Detection and Staging.
papers.summary: CEFA-Net, a knowledge-guided deep learning framework integrating clinical EEG biomarkers with raw multichannel EEG, was proposed for automated dementia detection and staging. On the CAUEEG dataset (1379 recordings), it achieved 81.02% accuracy for three-class dementia staging and 87.15% for abnormality detection, outperforming baselines by 6.75–9.10 percentage points, and improved MCI detection to 78% F1-score.

papers.title: Re-evaluating impaired consciousness in temporal lobe epilepsy: The role of language dominance and network reorganization.
papers.summary: This retrospective study analyzed 40 adults with temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) using video-EEG and language fMRI to assess the association between seizure onset laterality relative to language dominance and impaired consciousness. Bayesian estimation showed a 97.4% posterior probability that ipsilateral onset is associated with higher rate of focal impaired consciousness, but no significant task-evoked functional network connectivity differences were found between impairment groups.

papers.title: Spatial-Frequency Hypergraph Neural Network for EEG-fNIRS Emotion Recognition.
papers.summary: Proposes a Spatial-Frequency Hypergraph Neural Network (SF-HGNN) for EEG-fNIRS emotion recognition that uses dynamic frequency band decomposition, multi-scale temporal convolution, adaptive hypergraph convolution, and cross-modal attention. On the ENTER dataset, it achieved 82.94% subject-dependent and 68.85% subject-independent accuracy.

papers.title: Multi-Domain Feature Fusion and Channel Attention in an Inception-Based Architecture for Motor Imagery EEG Decoding.
papers.summary: Introduces an SE-EEG-Inception model with multi-domain feature fusion for motor imagery EEG decoding, using a dataset from 292 participants. It achieved mean 4-class accuracy of 89.4% and binary accuracies of 88.3% (arm) and 90.0% (leg).

papers.title: Mixture-of-Experts Electroencephalography-Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Fusion for Interpretable Computer-Assisted Brain Disorder Diagnosis.
papers.summary: BrainMoE, an adaptive EEG-fMRI fusion framework using modality-specific and shared neural-state experts with soft routing, was evaluated on the Healthy Brain Network dataset across five binary brain disorder classification tasks. It achieved an average AUC of 86.9 ± 3.0%, outperforming state-of-the-art algorithms, and provided ROI-level interpretability consistent with prior neuroimaging findings.

papers.title: From EEG Source Localization to Brain Network Analysis: A Computational Neuroscience Perspective.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the computational framework for EEG source localization and its transition to brain network analysis, covering forward and inverse problems, source reconstruction, functional and effective connectivity, graph-theoretical modeling, and machine learning applications. It highlights clinical uses, methodological challenges such as source leakage and reproducibility, and future directions for robust, clinically translatable source-level EEG analysis.

papers.title: From Oscillations to Brain States: Real-Time EEG-TMS for Adaptive Neuromodulation.
papers.summary: Reviews real-time EEG-TMS for adaptive neuromodulation, highlighting the shift from local mu-rhythm phase to whole-brain network-level state estimation using EEG source reconstruction and machine/deep learning. It discusses progress, limitations, and future directions toward network-targeted stimulation, illustrated by a chronic pain use case.

papers.title: The Cortical Source of the P300 ERP Generator in the Associative Learning Task: A Consensus of Four Inversion Algorithms.
papers.summary: This study localized the cortical generators of the P300 event-related potential during an associative learning task in 148 participants aged 7–21 using a consensus of four EEG source inversion algorithms. A convergence was found for cue onset-locked activity in the right inferior parietal lobule/angular gyrus and feedback-locked activity in occipital, temporal (including bilateral middle temporal gyrus), and orbitofrontal regions, with no age-related effects surviving the consensus criterion.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Microstate Dynamics as Neurophysiological Biomarkers Across the Alzheimer's Disease Continuum: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized 26 primary studies on resting-state EEG microstate dynamics across the Alzheimer's disease continuum (SCD, MCI, AD dementia) and their relation to AT(N) biomarkers. It identified graded group-level differences, including increased microstate A duration/coverage at MCI and AD stages, reduced microstate D parameters at MCI, and mixed findings for microstate C, but concluded that evidence is preliminary due to cross-sectional designs and limited pathological confirmation.

papers.title: Effects of MRI-Navigated Intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation on Task Performance, Subjective Workload, and EEG Responses During Prolonged Simulated Flight: A Randomized Crossover Study.
papers.summary: This randomized, order-balanced, within-subject crossover study examined the effects of MRI-navigated intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex on performance, workload, and EEG during a 60-minute simulated flight in 25 healthy men. Active iTBS improved composite performance scores in later phases and reduced NASA-TLX workload in phase 3, with relative reductions in frontocentral theta and fronto-parieto-occipital alpha power, but the authors caution that results are preliminary.

papers.title: Dual imagery tasks for EEG-based brain-computer interfaces: a feasibility study of combinatorial mental state classification.
papers.summary: This feasibility study introduced dual imagery (DI) tasks—combining singing imagery with motor imagery of one hand or both feet—to expand the number of distinguishable mental states for EEG-based brain-computer interfaces. Using filter bank common spatial patterns and regularized LDA on data from 14 healthy participants, classification accuracies reached 64.1% for 3-class and 63.0% for 4-class scenarios, with 7- and 8-class accuracies around 55% and 50%, demonstrating feasibility but not yet practical utility for high-command BCIs.

papers.title: Electroencephalographic Aspects in a Sheep with Coenurosis.
papers.summary: This case report characterized EEG and quantitative EEG (qEEG) findings in a 2-year-old sheep with chronic focal encephalopathy due to a Coenurus cerebralis cyst in the left cerebral hemisphere confirmed by CT, necropsy, and histopathology. It reports the first electrophysiological characterization of ovine coenurosis, showing a reproducible occipital qEEG asymmetry over the right hemisphere contralateral to the cyst despite no structural lesion there, interpreted as an electrophysiological false localizing sign arising mainly from signal attenuation over the diseased hemisphere.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence for Precision Antiarrhythmic Drug Therapy in Atrial Fibrillation: From Recurrence Prediction to Comparative Treatment Selection.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines artificial intelligence, machine learning, computational electrophysiology, and cardiac digital twins for precision antiarrhythmic drug therapy in atrial fibrillation. It highlights that ML models can predict drug-induced QT prolongation and that digital twins can simulate amiodarone responses, but most applications remain retrospective and models estimating outcomes under alternative AADs are still missing.

papers.title: Transdiagnostic EEG Signatures in ASD and ADHD: A Comparative Review of Computational Biomarkers and Neuromodulatory Interventions.
papers.summary: This comparative review synthesized 68 peer-reviewed studies (2010-2026) to compare EEG signatures across ASD and ADHD from a transdiagnostic perspective and to examine how such signatures might inform non-pharmacological intervention selection. Shared features included low-frequency theta excess, reduced alpha modulation under cognitive load, and flattened aperiodic 1/f slopes, while disorder-specific patterns comprised an ASD 'U-shaped' spectral profile with elevated epileptiform activity and frontally pronounced theta/beta ratio elevation in subsets of ADHD individuals; a biomarker-informed intervention-selection framework is proposed but requires prospective validation.

papers.title: The Effectiveness of a 6-Week Online Mindfulness-Based Intervention on Patients With Cervical Cancer or High-Grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion: A Randomized Controlled Trial Using Multimodal Data of Scales and Electroencephalogram.
papers.summary: A single-center randomized controlled trial of 151 cervical cancer or HSIL patients found that a 6-week online mindfulness-based intervention significantly reduced depressive (t=12.238, FDR-q<0.001) and anxiety (t=11.150, FDR-q<0.001) symptoms and increased resilience, mindfulness, and social support compared to general mental health education. Exploratory EEG showed higher relative theta and alpha power and lower beta and gamma power in the intervention group.

papers.title: Temporal Dynamics of Ensemble Face Representations Under Magnocellular- and Parvocellular-Biased Visual Inputs: A Time-Resolved EEG Decoding Study.
papers.summary: This time-resolved EEG decoding study with 24 healthy adults examined when ensemble face-gender information can be decoded under magnocellular-biased (low-luminance-contrast grayscale) and parvocellular-biased (isoluminant red-green) stimuli during a two-alternative forced-choice gender judgment task. M-biased ensemble gender information was reliably decodable in early (95-300 ms) and late (775-930 ms) windows with early temporal generalization, whereas P-biased ensembles showed no significant cluster-corrected time-resolved decoding but significant middle-to-late temporal generalization, indicating multistage temporal organization of ensemble face-gender information.

papers.title: Effects of Two Different Multicomponent Cognitive-Motor Training Protocols on EEG Spectral Activity, Cognitive-Motor Interference, and Gait Performance in Individuals with Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial assigned 44 chronic stroke participants to 4 weeks of either Progressive Task-Complexity Gait Training (PTCGT) or Constant Task-Complexity Gait Training (CTCGT) using the same auditory-feedback walker, assessing EEG spectral activity, cognitive-motor interference, and gait. Significant group-by-time interactions were observed for EEG and gait measures, with PTCGT showing greater pre-post changes in EEG spectral characteristics and gait performance than CTCGT; however, the DTC% interaction was significant in repeated-measures ANOVA (p=0.041) but not in mixed-effects sensitivity analysis (p=0.088), and cognitive-task performance was not quantitatively assessed, so dual-task improvement cannot be established.

papers.title: Nonconvulsive and Electrographic Status Epilepticus in Comatose Adult Survivors of Cardiac Arrest: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Prevalence, EEG-Based Diagnosis, Treatment, and Neurological Outcomes.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 17 studies estimated that strict nonconvulsive/electrographic/post-anoxic status epilepticus occurred in 22% of EEG-monitored comatose adult survivors of cardiac arrest. Pooled poor neurological outcome and mortality were 91% and 87%, respectively, though recovery occurred in selected patients with favorable EEG features.

papers.title: Iron Deficiency and Human Brain Electrophysiology Across the Lifespan: A Systematic and Mechanistic Review of Resting EEG, Event-Related Potentials, and Treatment Responsiveness.
papers.summary: This systematic and mechanistic review synthesized 30 human reports spanning the neonatal period to adulthood on EEG and event-related potential findings associated with iron deficiency and iron-deficiency anemia, and evaluated electrophysiological changes after iron treatment. Iron deficiency was commonly associated with increased slow-wave activity, reduced alpha activity, delayed sensory and cognitive processing, prolonged P300 and N2 latencies, altered frontal alpha asymmetry, and impaired differentiation of relevant versus irrelevant stimuli, with variable improvement after iron supplementation and some abnormalities persisting after hematological correction; no specific electrophysiological biomarker can currently be established.

papers.title: Investigating Neuropharmacological Features of the Cortical Activity of Cannabidiol GWP42003 P-A Phase 1 Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover Phase 1 trial, a single 1500 mg oral dose of purified cannabidiol (GWP42003-P) in 15 healthy males produced no statistically significant changes in widespread cortical excitability measured by TMS-EEG/EMG. A transient reduction in beta-band desynchronization at peak plasma concentration suggested a subtle, non-classical neuromodulatory effect.

papers.title: Decoding Bitter Taste Perception in Medicine-Food Homology Substances: A Multimethod Data and Sensory Assessment Approach.
papers.summary: A multimethod study using E-nose, sensory evaluation, E-tongue, GC-IMS, and EEG characterized bitterness perception in five medicine-food homology extracts (Chenpi, Lotus leaf, Sichuan pepper, Gardenia, American ginseng). It found discrepancies between perceived and chemically measured bitterness, distinct volatile fingerprints, and scalp EEG patterns with low-frequency activity for several bitter extracts and a delayed broadband increase for Sichuan pepper.

papers.title: Effects of Virtual Pedagogical Agents and Instructional Content Type on Learners' Experience in Online Learning: Evidence from Behavioral, Eye-Tracking, and EEG Data.
papers.summary: This study combined questionnaires, eye-tracking, and EEG in 40 university students to test how virtual pedagogical agent type (human-like vs. non-human) and instructional content type (traditional knowledge vs. interest-oriented popular science) affect online learning. Results showed a significant interaction: human-like agents improved learning experience for traditional content, whereas non-human agents led to better knowledge recall for interest-oriented content, with psychological distance and emotional attachment as mediators.

papers.title: Empathic Concern for Violators Modulates Victims' Evaluation of Third-Party Punishment Outcomes: Behavioral and EEG Evidence.
papers.summary: Using an adapted Third-Party Dictator Game with EEG, this study found that induced empathic concern for violators modulated victims' evaluations of third-party punishment outcomes. Empathy led to higher appropriateness ratings for no- and partial-punishment and lower for complete punishment, accompanied by reduced P2 for partial punishment, larger LPP for no punishment, and weaker parietal alpha suppression.

papers.title: Retinal Features and Preserved Vision in ENPP1 Deficiency: Long-Term Insights from Multimodal Imaging and Electrophysiology.
papers.summary: This longitudinal single-case study used multimodal ophthalmic imaging and electrophysiology to assess a male patient with ENPP1 deficiency over ten years. Despite systemic ectopic calcification, retinal structure and function remained largely preserved, with only mild subclinical changes including reduced ERG amplitudes and rod sensitivity, suggesting electrophysiology as a candidate noninvasive monitoring biomarker.

papers.title: Iatrogenic Dextrose Hyperosmolar Extravasation Injury in Suspected Endogenous Hyperinsulinism.
papers.summary: A case report of a 44-year-old woman with suspected endogenous hyperinsulinism who developed iatrogenic dextrose hyperosmolar extravasation injury after prolonged peripheral infusion of 10% dextrose. The injury presented as progressive tense bullae on the right forearm, highlighting the risk of insidious soft tissue injury from sustained high-concentration dextrose through peripheral catheters.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
